> A DIY tiny handheld console using a 1.3 inch oled and an esp32-c3 supermini with 6 input buttons and buzzer for sound. Includes a battery and protected charging mechanism. The PCB is approximately 80 × 85 mm, or 8 × 8.5 cm, so its fairly easy to carry. Includes a few games for now and you can add more later!

## Design

### 2026-11-07: **NOVEMBER 6: I finished the schematic and pcb routing (Basically the hardware designing part)**

**6h**

**NOVEMBER 6: I finished the schematic and pcb routing (Basically the hardware designing part)**

I finished up the schematic and the pcb placement and routing for the board!

I decided to use a esp32 c3 supermini as the microprocessor since its small and where i live the XIAO wasn't available locally so i went with this. And instead of a standard 0.96" oled, i went with a 1.3" oled since bigger screen is better for games i think. I also finally decided to use the grouped schematic into different parts rather than just making a mess in the middle, and I think I am actually enjoying this stuff!
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/8e2880018aa1f9ec60e6073f1f7c963f0b0407ed9b973a66388fcc837deaa36d.png)
So at first I had so much issues. My main issue was I was a beginner right, this is my first non tutorial project and I tried to start with the schematic and I couldnt find a esp32 c3 supermini symbol at all. And I tried to use some other like a wroom esp32 whatever that means (im still new to all this) and it looked nothing like the esp32 supermini. I was so lost on what to even start with the power section looked scary, display too, and all. I almost quit, but then i thought and i went to SnapEDA found the modules symbol and footprints, and after that it was smooth sailing. I found the microprocessor, the oled, and the tp4506 (i had to make this symbol myself, i did find a footprint online but no symbol so i diyed it)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/20ce63e75a62e093c10bc39ad2cb2573abf3ed60a1bf84a7472d5014e7dad806.png)

And once i actually got those symbols it was so much easy to know what I was doing and I got the schematic working and done in around 2.5 Hours.

**Now the PCB**

I had designed a pcb before for the week 1 project, but that was a tutorial project so PCB was also slightly complicated for me, but it was lowkey more fun than the schematic since the 3d render looks so cool like its actually comming together and all.
![image 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/d7ab9cfb3e8068adcb73a2c95f0be1058d60b0ab8fa0b8ceda4a8551318ea67a.png)

![image 2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/234b6d6ace2227943c1d488c49101bb8898937429c45cde4540502af5ce73291.png)

And this time I think the traces are better. I mean its not that impressive compared to others but for me , this is my second pcb design and im proud of it.

I first started with roughly putting the components where i wanted then fixing on a shape.

I first thought of like that slant you see on the pcb on the top only left and right, but once i put the esp i realised that dosent really work so i went for this cool little design i think it looks good.

And I remember week 1 my project was sent back once and one suggestion I got was to use a ground plane, so i did that first off all this time on both sides which made my ratsnest much cleaner and made it less overwhelming.
![image 3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/dfd1482bd8dd8b58095171b29e45199d24a448b3f63e7cabca836c3c5fc6a074.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/b558541733330c16d9402f45bc311621369633d02b9d9525224d2d04e477eed3.png)
Then i put the display and buttons on the front side of the pcb and the other parts the battery, charger, capacitors, resistors, buzzer, and esp on the back side
Once i was happy with the placement I traced those out as best as i could to try and make it not messy.

I changes the placements up a few times and now this is the final one, Im happy with it. (I also added testpoints since I heard thats good practice)

I ran both ERC and DRC and both came out clean so this should work hopefully.

Time taken on pcb it was 3.5 hours.

**Total time spent = 6 hours**

*Overall it was a productive session, once i got the proper symbols it was smooth sailing with only a few hiccups like a messy ratsnest, or confusion during placement, but now im 50% done with the project , and ill work on the software part now :) *

### 2026-11-08: **November 7 and 8: Finished the software designing part, so essentially im done with the designing week**

**6.5h**

**November 7 and 8: Finished the software designing part, so essentially im done with the designing week**

*Now i just need to finish up the github, create a BOM and submit*

So I said how i was recommended to code the games in seperate .h files and config files, sound, menu and all too. So I did it. Theres 16 total files in the folder for the software. The main one is Handheld.ino which essentially connects everything.

Then theres 5 files for 5 games.
I planned on six but pacman was getting too hard to code and when i tried to review the code using Claude, it said there were issues and it told me something to fix the issue which i didnt understand at all. The AI of the ghosts were complex, and i tried to create a randomized map but i couldnt, so i just dropped that idea for now and decided to make five games.![20261108_142242](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/0e54c3a05d7fec67648abf5e3b3d4b46f6fb6c10be3712fa6243ab8291e9caf5.jpg) Pong, Space shooter, Street racer, Snake, and Brick breaker.

*Each game is named and designed different than generic, you can see if you look through the code*

And then theres other files:
config.h, sound.h, menu.h, gamebase.h, icons.h, gfx.h, boot.h, hwtest.h, games.h, input.h.

Which all have different functions (The functions are pretty aparent from the file names)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/fcb0bf69081a68ce888a28d504de18a0c1db05b19d146c6f2e103555b8b599b5.png)
**The actual code**

I wrote the code for all the config files, and the games.
I looked at some premade games that were available, saw what they were doing, asked Claude to help on where to start then started to write the program.

I initialised the I2C for the oled, and first wrote a hardware testing code, so once i get the grant and get the items, i can test everything before I upload the program so testing is easier.

Then I wrote the Input, gamebase and games files. These are basiclaly the common things every game I wrote shares like the gameover screen and the highscore and current score tab in the top.

I first wrote Snake, Then tried pacman but then it got too hard so i dropped that and switched to a street racer style game but with boats, then a space shooter but with zombies and guns, and Pong, and a brick breaker game.
![20261108_142407](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/JAJv8CpYXEK3ozEdCWum90HeDDPojsUr/562dee42cec1b237fb16ba5eed03cb3694e9333aeec9bd0011fd81da403d6cc1.jpg)
